concepts.def: IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.
Brainstorming, SCAMPER, mood boards and morphological charts produce divergent ideas; convergence selects strongest concept.
Low-fidelity (paper, foam, cardboard) progresses through mid-fidelity (3D-printed) to high-fidelity working models; feedback drives refinement.
UK Design Council 2005 process: discover and define (problem), develop and deliver (solution); two divergent-convergent diamonds.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Classic Design — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Classic Design brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Classic Design.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 2005 Double Diamond models the design process?
options: IDEO
UK Design Council
Stanford d.school
Frog Design

mcqs.q: Which technique systematically alters product attributes?
options: SCAMPER
TRIZ
PMI
SWOT

mcqs.q: Why is injection moulding suited to high-volume production?
options: It is the cheapest method for any quantity.
How long the tree took to grow.
Tooling cost is high but per-unit cost is very low at scale.
It is the only way to make plastic items.

mcqs.q: Why do designers often use 5th to 95th percentile data instead of just the 50th?
options: It is the only way to make plastic items.
Because law requires it.
To accommodate the majority of users rather than just the average.
Because the 50th percentile is too unreliable.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a timber is a hardwood or softwood?
options: Because law requires it.
How long the tree took to grow.
Whether the wood itself is physically hard or soft.
The type of tree - deciduous (hardwood) or coniferous (softwood), not its hardness.
